key_insight: PIWF splits multiscale fluid fields into global Fourier modes and localized wavelet features, then fuses them in a physics-informed network to better capture both smooth trends and sharp gradients.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical surrogate modeling strategy for CFD problems with shocks, fronts, wakes, and vortices when dense interior data are unavailable.
method: Fourier branch models long-range coherent flow structures.
Wavelet branch captures compact, localized steep-gradient and vortical features.
Residual MLP with channel attention fuses both branches under PDE, initial, and boundary constraints.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on five canonical problems—Burgers, shallow water, Kovasznay flow, Taylor--Green vortex, and 2D cylinder wake—showing improved resolution of shocks, wet-dry fronts, wakes, vortices, and spectra versus PINNs and PI-KANs.
watch_item: The added branch fusion and attention may increase model complexity and tuning effort, so performance and stability should be checked carefully across new flow regimes.
paper_title: Physics informed wavelet Fourier representation for multiscale fluid dynamics
